description:
🔌 **EVALUATE ADOPTING BEFORE BUILDING (2026-08-13 portfolio scan).** The worktree-orchestration category grew substantially since this was authored — ccswarm, Spec-Kitty, parallel-code, agentree, git-worktree-runner — and the survey finding is directly on this tasklist's subject: *"parallel agents can create merge conflicts between themselves without knowing, and no tool warns you when two agents might edit the same code"*, yet **some tools now predict conflicts between worktrees before they happen and warn when two agents are about to overlap on the same function or class.** That is a strictly finer instrument than a `touches` tag, and it is adjacent rather than competing — per the standing principle in `rosetta/strategy/DECISIONS.md` — *a competitor at your layer is a threat; a competitor at an adjacent layer is a socket.* Evaluate binding one before building the registry. **But weigh it honestly:** chief's `touches` model is coarse and therefore cheap, predictive tools are young, and a predictor that is wrong in either direction is worse than a hint an operator already distrusts. This session produced live evidence for both sides — `280`'s `touches` were CONCEPTUAL TAGS (`cuneiform-engine`, `render-goldens`) that lexically match nothing, so the scheduler could not serialize it against anything, while `308`/`311` declared real paths and were correctly serialized on `ccl.rs`.

---

Chief's `touches` field lists the conflict domains the parallel scheduler serializes on — but it is ADVISORY by design, and the docs say so plainly: the merge floor (rebase → re-verify → --no-ff) is the correctness guarantee, tags are a hint. That was a defensible call when the only risk being managed was textual conflict. The independent 2026 scaling research names a second risk the merge floor does NOT catch: parallel agents each hold a different slice of context, so they produce 'individually correct code that breaks when combined' — a green rebase and a green verify on each branch says nothing about whether the two branches' designs agree. The recommended mitigation is an OVERLAP ZONE REGISTRY: a declared set of high-impact files/services where a change triggers MANDATORY human review regardless of automated results. That is `touches`, promoted from hint to policy. The same research supplies the other half: the AgenticFlict dataset finds larger diffs correlate with higher conflict probability, so 'controlling change size is the lever' — chief currently has no size budget per story at all. This tasklist adds both: a per-repo overlap-zone registry that can force review on designated domains, and a per-story diff-size budget that flags oversized changes. Neither weakens the merge floor; both add a policy layer above it. Scope: `engine/driver.sh` (scheduler + merge phase), `.chief/config` + `templates/`, `docs/drivers-and-safety.md`. See ../AGENTIC-ENGINEERING-ADVISORY.md §2.6 and §5.

userStories.title: Adopt or build — decide on evidence
userStories.description: Added by the 2026-08-13 scan. A finer instrument may already exist; check before building the registry.
acceptanceCriteria: At least two worktree conflict-prediction tools are assessed for whether they can be BOUND behind chief's existing `touches` seam rather than replacing it — the registry could consume a predictor's verdict instead of a hand-declared tag.

The measured failure mode is stated as the acceptance bar: a tasklist whose `touches` are conceptual TAGS rather than paths (`280` declared `cuneiform-engine`, `render-goldens`) is invisible to lexical matching, so any adopted or built mechanism must catch that case or it fixes nothing.
A DECLINE is recorded with its reason — coarse-but-cheap is a legitimate answer, and this tasklist's own premise is that the merge floor is the correctness guarantee.

userStories.title: An overlap-zone registry that can force review
userStories.description: Let a repo declare high-impact domains where a green gate is not sufficient authority to merge.
acceptanceCriteria: A per-repo registry (in `.chief/config` or a sibling file, documented) declares overlap zones as path patterns and/or `touches` domain names, each with a policy: `serialize` (today's behavior) or `review` (serialize AND require explicit human approval before merge)

A tasklist whose branch modifies a `review`-policy zone does NOT auto-merge on a green verify: it lands in a distinct awaiting-approval state, visible in `chief ps`/`monitor`, and merges only on explicit approval — the merge floor still runs first, so approval is asked for a branch that is already rebased and green, never instead of the gate
Approval is recorded durably and survives process death (a restart must not re-ask for an approval already granted), consistent with chief's filesystem-resumable model

When `89`'s plan-review checkpoint is enabled for the same tasklist, the two do not double-prompt: an overlap-zone approval and a plan approval are distinct decisions at distinct times, and the docs state which is asked when

userStories.title: A per-story diff-size budget
userStories.description: Large diffs raise conflict probability and are the thing the research says to control; make oversize visible and optionally blocking.
acceptanceCriteria: A configurable per-story diff-size budget (changed lines and/or changed files, per repo, with a documented default) is evaluated at commit/merge time; exceeding it is surfaced in the story's record and in `ps`/`monitor` output

The budget's ENFORCEMENT is configurable: warn (default) or block-pending-approval — a hard block by default would break legitimate large refactors, so the default must not be obstructive while still making oversize visible

The check reads the branch's real diff against `$CHIEF_BASE_BRANCH` (the same scope the verify hook uses), so a story that touches many files legitimately (a rename sweep) can be distinguished in the message from one that grew unbounded

Guidance in `docs/` connects the budget to the vertical-slice principle: prefer several small end-to-end stories over one horizontal layer-at-a-time story, citing that reviewing 100-200 lines and resteering is far cheaper than reviewing 2,000+

userStories.title: Document the policy layer and pin it with tests
userStories.description: The safety model doc must state clearly what is a guarantee and what is a policy.
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/drivers-and-safety.md` gains an overlap-zone section that PRESERVES the existing honest framing (the merge floor is the correctness guarantee; `touches` remains a scheduling hint) and adds the new layer above it: zones with a `review` policy are a deliberate human gate for cross-branch design divergence, which no automated gate detects

A hermetic test asserts: a branch touching a `serialize`-policy zone behaves exactly as today (no regression); a branch touching a `review`-policy zone rebases, verifies green, then WAITS for approval and merges only after it; a granted approval survives a simulated restart; an oversized diff is flagged under `warn` and withheld under `block`
